convention: World axes are Blender's (Z up). The creature faces -Y. Its LEFT is world +X and its RIGHT is world -X (the three tails stack on +x, the figure's left; the front camera sees +X on the image right). 'left' and 'right' in a camera id always mean the creature's own side, and the camera sits on that side: side-left looks at the creature's left flank from +X, threequarter-left stands at front-left (+X, -Y). A camera is its target plus an offset (the direction from the target to the camera, any length that clears the figure); it looks at the target along the negative offset with world +Z up (the top and below cameras use a 0.001 y offset so the up vector stays defined). All cameras are orthographic, so orthoScale is the width and height of the frame in world units.
figureFrame: Whole-figure cameras use the species' fixed render frame (species.json frame.render: center 0.0287, 0.1647, -0.0300; scale 3.1981), the frame every Akinza assembly render has used, so the figure never rescales between builds. Top and below use a tighter scale on the figure's plan centre.
headFrame: Head close cameras are in world coordinates around the head as the assembly places it (head scale .5, offset 0, -.02, .635); targets and scales are those of render_clay_views.py w-front, w-back, w-top, w-side and w-tq, which are the views the head reviews used.

lightRig.note: Three area lamps aimed at a fixed point (the whole-creature bounds centre of the Akinza assemblies). They are placed in world space and never move with a camera, so every view of every build is lit alike. Offsets are from the aim point.
